title: Nifty 50 returns in the last 10 years: year-by-year table and CAGR
dek: Ten calendar years, all positive, and about 12.6% a year before dividends. Then 2026 so far: down 13.5% with two months to go.
author: sarah-qureshi

body.title: Key numbers
items: About 12.6% a year over 10 years: 7,946 at the end of 2015 to 26,130 at the end of 2025, price index only
About 13.0% a year over 3 years and 13.3% a year over 5 years
Best year 2017 (+28.65%); weakest 2016 (+3.01%); all ten years from 2016 to 2025 ended higher

body.text: The Nifty 50 returned about 12.6% a year over the last 10 years, from 7,946 at the end of 2015 to 26,130 at the end of 2025. That is the price index alone, before dividends. Every one of those ten calendar years finished higher than it started.

body.caption: Nifty 50 calendar-year price return. Source: NSE closing levels; returns calculated by India in Data.

body.text: The 10-year average hides a wide spread. The best year was 2017 at +28.65%. The weakest was 2016 at +3.01%, and two other years (2018 and 2022) also returned less than 5%. In 2020 the index fell almost 40% from its January high to its March low, and still ended the year up 14.9%.
Nifty annual returns over 3, 5 and 10 years

Measured to the end of 2025 on the price index, the Nifty 50 compounded at about 13.0% a year over 3 years (2022 to 2025), 13.3% over 5 years (2020 to 2025) and 12.6% over 10 years (2015 to 2025). These are our calculations from the year-end closing levels in the table above, before dividends.

Put simply, ₹1 lakh invested at the end of 2015 would have grown to about ₹3.29 lakh by the end of 2025 on price alone. The calendar-year Nifty returns above range from +3.01% (2016) to +28.65% (2017).

These are price returns. The Nifty 50 total return index adds the dividends paid by index companies, so it runs higher than the price index. Returns also depend on the start and end dates: the same index measured from the end of 2016 or the end of 2017 gives a different average.
The 2015 start matters too. The index fell 4.06% that year, so a 10-year window starting from the 2015 close begins from a low base.

At 22,600 on 23 October, the Nifty 50 is 13.5% below its 2025 year-end close of 26,130. If it finishes the year below that level, it would be the first down calendar year since 2015, ending a run of ten straight gains. There are still two months of trading left, so the final figure will differ.
The average return is a destination. No single year is obliged to take you there directly.

items.q: What is the Nifty 50 return in the last 10 years?
items.a: About 12.6% a year on the price index, from 7,946 at the end of 2015 to 26,130 at the end of 2025. That excludes dividends.

items.q: What were the Nifty 50 yearly returns from 2016 to 2025?
How is the 10-year annual return calculated?
items.a: It is the compound annual growth rate: the year-end 2025 level divided by the year-end 2015 level, raised to the power of one tenth, minus one.
No. These are price returns. The Nifty 50 total return index adds dividends, so it runs higher.

body.text: Sources: year-end closing levels for 2015 to 2023 from Forbes India’s Nifty 50 history table, the 2025 close and annual gain from Samco’s calendar-year review, 2024 and 2026 levels from NSE data. Annual returns and the 12.6% compound rate are our calculations from those closing levels.
